messages.subject: Error of non-numeric argument to binary operator
messages.subject_clean: Error of non-numeric argument to binary operator
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I am getting the following error message with many of the DartR functions.
"Error in p1/p2 : non-numeric argument to binary operator".

This error appeared with most gl.filter functions (e.g. gl.filter.reproducibility, gl.filter.callrate, gl.filter.maf ) and also with gl.dist.pop.

My DartR version: 2.9.7 and I am working on Rstudio with R version 4.4.1.
I have tried the followings to troubleshoot but in all cases the same error-message appeared.
-  Tried the above commands using the testset.gl <http://testset.gl>
-  Installed the dartR and other necessary packages using:
             install.packages("dartR")
             library(dartR)
             install.packages("devtools")
             gl.install.vanilla.dartR()

   -  I have also tried the dartR functions by installing the developmental version of dartR.

Any suggestions, what might be the issue and how to fix?
Thank you !
Almas

messages.subject: Re: Error of non-numeric argument to binary operator
messages.subject_clean: Error of non-numeric argument to binary operator
messages.body_plain:
Hi Almas,

If you have a genlight/dartR object in your environment, Rstudio will automatically load the library that created that object and the installation will fail. To avoid this, please install the developing version of dartR in an Rstudio session with an empty Environment.

Here is a link about how you can clear your environment:
Clear the Console and the Environment in R Studio - GeeksforGeeks <https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/clear-the-console-and-the-environment-in-r-studio/>

Alternatively, if you don't want to remove all your variables and objects from your environment, you can create a new Rstudio project just for this installation.

Please use the below commands to install the developing version of dartR.base and the package patchwork:

devtools::install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR.base@dev")
install.packages("patchwork")

Cheers,
Luis

messages.subject: Error in creating PCOA plot
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I am trying to run PCA and PCOA analyses and create the plots using the to use gl.pcoa and gl.pcoa.plot functions. While I could successfully create the PCA plot, I get some error message with the PCOA plot. I am using "dev" version of DartRverse.

Here is what I have tried:
# PCA (without specifying any genetic distance matrix)
pcoa <- gl.pcoa(gl_flt)
gl.pcoa.plot(pcoa, gl_flt)    # creating PCA plot

The above command successfully created PCA plot showing the individuals and population names.

# PCOA (with nei's genetic distance)
dnei <- gl.dist.pop(gl_flt, method="nei")
pcoa2 <- gl.pcoa(dnei)
gl.pcoa.plot(pcoa2, gl_flt)

Starting gl.pcoa.plot   Processing an ordination file (glPca)  Processing genlight object with SNP data Error in data.frame(..., check.names = FALSE) :
arguments imply differing number of rows: 9, 266

Any suggestions what might be the problem here?
gl.compliance.check(gl_flt)  shows "population assignment confirmed".
So this cannot be the issue as was described as a potential cause in a previous conversation.

Thank you!
Almas

messages.subject: Low call rate and very low loci after filtering
messages.subject_clean: Low call rate and very low loci after filtering
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have 94 individuals of an annual daisy collected across
12 populations (~8 indiv. per population). These populations are spread across
isolated remnants along a 150 km sampling transect. For SNP data, individuals
missing data range from 0.23 to 0.63, reporting call rate by individual yields
~32,000 loci (median call rate ~0.44). After filtering for secondaries with a
threashold of 0.9, I ended up with 329 loci. While doing a PCoA on this, the
axes explain combined ~5%.

This is my first time using SNP data and DArT and my
results are very different colleagues doing similar work. We sent the samples
for DNA extraction and sequencing and I am wondering if this is a problem with
low DNA quality/extraction issues or whether it is a problem with the species?
Any advice you have would be greatly appreciated.

Manuel

messages.body_plain:
Hi Almas,

Based on the genlight object and the code that you shared with me, I found that the problem is that you are calculating the distance between two populations, PCA requires at least three pairwise distances, i.e. at least three populations.

Cheers,
Luis

messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Low call rate and very low loci after filtering
messages.subject_clean: [dartR] Low call rate and very low loci after filtering
messages.body_plain:
The only way to really know is to ask DArT for their advice on the
quality of the DNA extracted or any other issues they had. They take
pictures of every step so it is all very carefully documented.

When you plot missing loci do you get an even looking plot, or something
bimodal looking (i.e., multiple peaks)?

I would also try doing a light filtering and running a tree to check
that you don't have some quirky samples in there that might be quite
different.  Tree type analyses aren't as impacted by missing data.
Usually you can get away with running a neighbour joining tree (although
sometimes these can produce quirky results, but usually they are okay).

Cheers
Peter Unmack

messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Low call rate and very low loci after filtering
messages.subject_clean: [dartR] Low call rate and very low loci after filtering
messages.body_plain:
Hi Manuel,

Thanks for sharing the list of filters you used (see below).

gl_waitzia <- gl.filter.callrate(gl_waitzia, method = "loc", threshold = 0.95)
gl_waitzia <- gl.filter.rdepth(gl_waitzia, lower = 10, upper = 100)
gl_waitzia <- gl.filter.reproducibility(gl_waitzia, threshold = 0.99)
gl_waitzia <- gl.filter.monomorphs(gl_waitzia)

Your filter thresholds are not that stringent, but you ended up with quite a few loci. It is likely that your samples had a low quantity/quality DNA. As Peter mentioned, you could ask DArT for a summary of the DNA of your samples.

However, if you use less stringent thresholds, you will still get good quality SNPs. For example, you could use a minimum threshold for read depth of 5 and not using an upper threshold or using a call rate of 0.80. You could also first filter those samples with the most missing data and then filter missing data by loci.

You can find more information on filtering on our tutorials:

- Microsoft Word - Tutorial_5_dartR_Basic_Filtering_22-Dec-21 (2).doc (biomatix.org) <http://georges.biomatix.org/storage/app/media/uploaded-files/tutorial5dartrbasicfiltering22-dec-21-2.pdf>
- Session 2 Renee Catullo (youtube.com) <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UikEkCs-t4g&t=1537s>
- Kioloa PopGen - 1  Intro to dartR (green-striped-gecko.github.io) <https://green-striped-gecko.github.io/kioloa/session01.html>

You could also impute your missing data by using the function gl.impute.

What's more important, though, is to understand the implications of missing data and number of loci for each of the analyses you will perform.

Cheers,
Luis

messages.subject: Re: How to synchronize color set for grouping and clustering in plots produced by dartR
messages.subject_clean: How to synchronize color set for grouping and clustering in plots produced by dartR
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rizki,

Please find below some examples to synchronise colors across analyses.

Cheers,
Luis

########## USING SAME COLORS ACROSS ANALYSES #########
library(dartRverse)
t1 <- platypus.gl <http://platypus.gl>
#filtering
t1 <- gl.filter.callrate(t1,
                         threshold = 1)
t1 <- gl.filter.monomorphs(t1)
# select colors
pcolors <- gl.select.colors(library='baseR',
                            palette='rainbow',
                            ncolors = nPop(t1))
# PCA
pca <- gl.pcoa(t1)
# 2D plot
gl.pcoa.plot(glPca = pca,
             x = t1,
             pt.colors = pcolors)
# 3D plot
gl.pcoa.plot(glPca = pca,
             x = t1,
             pt.colors = pcolors,
             zaxis = 3)
# GRM
g1 <- gl.grm(x = t1,
       palette_convergent = gl.colors(type = "con"),
       palette_discrete = pcolors)
# network
gl.grm.network(G = g1,
               x = t1,
               palette_discrete = pcolors)
# location map
gl.map.interactive(x = t1,
                   ind.circle.cols = pcolors[as.numeric(pop(t1))])
# heterozygosity
gl.report.heterozygosity(x = t1,
                         plot.colors.pop = pcolors)
# spatial autocorrelation
gl.spatial.autoCorr(x = t1,
                    plot.colors.pop = pcolors)
# LD vs distance
# assigning chromosome and SNP position
t1$chromosome <- t1$other$loc.metrics$Chrom_Platypus_Chrom_NCBIv1
t1$position <- t1$other$loc.metrics$ChromPos_Platypus_Chrom_NCBIv1
l1 <- gl.report.ld.map(t1,
                       ld.max.pairwise = 1e7)
gl.ld.distance(ld.report = l1,
               pop.colors = pcolors)
# effective population size
gl.LDNe(x= t1,
        plot_colors_pop = pcolors)
